newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Thailand committed to liberalisation, says Amnuay.
newsitem.headline: Thailand committed to liberalisation, says Amnuay.

text.p: Thailand remains committed to financial liberalisation, privatisation and decentralisation after last weekend's elections, deputy prime minister and foreign affairs minister Amnuay Viravan said on Monday.

"Policies of the new government will focus on stability over growth, which should result in seven to eight percent annual economic growth," Amnuay told delegates to a World Economic Forum meeting in Hong Kong on Monday.
Amnuay, who political analysts have said was widely expected to join a new coalition government to be formed by the New Aspiration Party as economics minister, said nothing had been decided yet.
"Chances are that I will accept it but will not be able to say definitely until I meet all coalition partners," he told a news conference after speaking at the forum.
The NAP edged out the Democratic Party by two seats in Sunday's elections. Amnuay confirmed he had spoken to leaders of the NAP about the economics post prior to the elections.
Amnuay said the new government would emphasise investment efficiency. He said Thailand "can no longer afford the political patronage system".
"There will be no white-elephant projects, no inflated values to the development activities. Every baht must be used wisely," he said.

Amnuay said Sunday's elections represented another step in the steady maturing of Thailand's democracy. He said key economic ministries would no longer be entrusted to influential but inexperienced members of parliament.

"All major parties have recruited qualified people, both elected and non-elected, to head economic teams," Amnuay said. "That ensures that no matter which party heads the government, capable ministers will be appointed."
